purpose: Personal-investment research for metals and cross-commodity resource exposures relevant to electrification, data-centre infrastructure, food security and nuclear fuel.

ideas.name: BHP Group ADR
ideas.thesis: BHP now deserves a place in Power Stack as a diversified resource platform rather than merely a broad miner. Copper has become its largest earnings engine, giving direct exposure to grid, electrification and data-centre demand; Jansen adds a food-security/potash leg from 2027; and Olympic Dam provides uranium by-product exposure. The diversification lowers single-project risk versus a pure copper developer while still leaning increasingly toward Power Stack bottlenecks.
ideas.catalysts: Sustained high copper prices, expansion at Escondida/Copper South Australia, a 2026 Vicuña Stage-1 investment decision, Jansen potash production beginning in 2027, further Olympic Dam expansion work and disciplined balance-sheet execution.
ideas.risks: Copper and iron-ore cyclicality, China/global growth exposure, Jansen potash execution after cost overruns and impairment, large-project capital discipline, labour/geopolitical risk and valuation rerating after strong copper performance.
ideas.valuationTechnical: BHP has already rerated as copper becomes a larger share of earnings, so this is not a hidden-value trade. The attraction is diversified cash generation plus copper/potash/uranium optionality. Prefer pullbacks or periods where copper earnings and project execution outpace multiple expansion.
ideas.researchNote: FY2026 results materially changed the mix: copper generated roughly 55% of group underlying EBITDA and overtook iron ore as the largest earnings contributor. BHP produced about 2 Mt of copper for a second consecutive year and is targeting major copper growth through the mid-2030s. Jansen remains on track to begin potash production in 2027, although recent impairment/cost overruns keep project discipline as the main counterweight.

categoryRead: Copper remains one of the cleanest cross-category Power Stack bottlenecks because it is required by grids, electrical equipment, data centres, renewables and industrial automation. BHP is promoted as the diversified core-quality expression; pure-play miners should still be judged separately for torque versus balance-sheet/project risk.
